thread:
megan: :rotating_light: Heads up — canary for release 2.5.0 in us-east is showing a sustained p95 latency spike and a small uptick in 5xxs since 08:12 UTC. Deploy-bot flagged it.

deploy-bot: automated alert: canary:us-east - p95 latency +45% over baseline for last 5m, error rate 0.9% (threshold 0.5%). Recommend hold.

sanjay: copying metrics, can we see which variant is affected? dedicated pool or hosted?

lena: looks like traffic routed to variant v2.5.0-quant on dedicated-us-east-1. Only ~8% of traffic.

megan: thanks. Given it's above our canary thresholds, we need to decide auto rollback vs manual. Are we seeing any request patterns tied to a customer?

tom: CS says one enterprise tenant reported intermittent failures around the same time. CS pinged me, they want a customer-facing note if we roll back.

megan: quick check — does rollback automation cover this variant? ops-bot?

ops-bot: rollback-automation: eligible=true, safety-checks=pass, required-owners=[eng-releases, oncall], ETA=~3m.

sanjay: I'm +1 for manual rollback + communication. Reason: dedicated pool for enterprise tenant — prefer human-in-loop to confirm traffic split and customer brief.

lena: agree. We should also pin traffic to previous stable (2.4.9) for that pool only instead of full cluster revert, to avoid impacting other regions.

megan: plan proposal: 1) hold further canaries, 2) pin dedicated-us-east-1 pool to 2.4.9, 3) run rollback of variant on that pool, 4) notify affected customer and post an incident note if errors persist. Who will execute?

tom: I can run the pin + rollback. Will coordinate with oncall.

sanjay: I'll prepare the customer note draft and postmortem checklist.

megan: command to run (ops runbook):
```
# pin pool and trigger targeted rollback
redwoodctl traffic pin --pool=dedicated-us-east-1 --model=core --version=2.4.9 --reason="canary instability"
redwoodctl deploy rollback --pool=dedicated-us-east-1 --service=core --to-version=2.4.9 --target=variant:v2.5.0-quant
```

megan: tom, annotate the deploy with :reason and ping @sanjay when done. We'll wait 5m after pin before rolling if traffic still stable.

tom: starting now. pin step done. output: 
```
INFO: traffic pinned to 2.4.9 for dedicated-us-east-1 (commit: a1b2c3)
```

tom: waiting 5m for stabilization then rollback.

(3m later)

deploy-bot: canary:us-east - p95 latency still +38%, error rate 0.7%.

sanjay: ok proceed with rollback. Customer note draft in #customer-success: "We're pausing the recent canary update for your dedicated pool and reverting to the prior stable version 2.4.9 while we investigate increased latencies. You may see brief reconnections; no data loss expected. We'll follow up with root cause and timeline."

megan: good. tom, run rollback and include step id in ticket.

tom: running rollback now: 
```
redwoodctl deploy rollback --pool=dedicated-us-east-1 --service=core --to-version=2.4.9 --force --tag=manual-rollback-2249999999
```

(1m)

tom: rollback completed. deploy-bot confirms: rollback success, all variant instances replaced with 2.4.9.

deploy-bot: rollout event: rollback completed for dedicated-us-east-1 at 09:06 UTC.

megan: monitoring — please watch p95 and 5xx for next 15m. Sanjay, send the customer note with the rollback timestamp and brief troubleshooting steps.

sanjay: sent to CS for review, posting now.

(10m later)

lena: metrics look good — p95 back to baseline, error rate down to 0.1%. No regressions in other regions.

megan: thanks team. Action items: 1) Sanjay to own customer comms and incident timeline, 2) Tom to update release notes + tag release as rolled back in changelog, 3) SRE to run postmortem check and link eval prompts that failed.

sanjay: on it, will include exact timestamps and who was notified.

tom: release notes updated: added entry "2.5.0 - partial rollback for dedicated-us-east-1 due to canary latency spike; reverting to 2.4.9". Pushed changelog commit f7e8d9.

megan: closing thread — we kept manual control which was the right call given dedicated customer. Marking as resolved for oncall; reopen if anomalies reappear. :thumbsup:
